children: Chesapeake Utilities said its indirect subsidiary Peninsula Pipeline Holdings has sold a minority interest in Florida Energy Pathway, a natural gas transmission infrastructure project in South Florida.
Under the agreement, Peninsula will retain 51% ownership of the project, and NextEra Energy Resources will buy a 49% minority ownership interest.
The joint venture engaged Chesapeake Utilities' subsidiary, Peninsula Pipeline Co., to construct, manage and operate the project.

The company said FEP is expected to be a 24-inch intrastate natural gas infrastructure project constructed from Palm Beach County to Miami-Dade County. The project is designed to expand natural gas transportation capacity, address regional supply constraints, meet growing customer demand, and enhance energy reliability in one of the nation's fastest-growing regions. Total project investment is estimated to be $1.2 billion, pending finalization of design and development activities.
Chesapeake said it expects construction to begin during the first half of 2028, and the project is anticipated to be in service in 2030, subject to final commissioning.
